n2f83965fbd3.s:
Consider the following statements about the grant to Balaputradeva's monastery at Nalanda:
1. The five villages were granted by Devapala.
2. The grant is recorded in the Nalanda copper plate.
3. The grant was made by Dharmapala, founder of Vikramashila.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n2f83965fbd3.x: Devapala granted the five villages, as the Nalanda copper plate records. Dharmapala founded Vikramashila but did not make this grant.

n3cdb41a016d.s: Somapura Mahavihara is located at present-day:
n3cdb41a016d.x: Somapura Mahavihara is at Paharpur in Naogaon district, Bangladesh. Antichak is Vikramashila, Varendra is Jagaddala and Bihar Sharif is Odantapuri.

n09357db0ff8.s:
Consider the following statements about the destruction of Pala-period centres of learning:
1. Their destruction by Bakhtiyar Khilji is generally placed around 1193–1200.
2. One tradition gives 1194 for the destruction of Nalanda.
3. Jagaddala was sacked in the early eleventh century.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n09357db0ff8.x: The destruction is placed around 1193–1200, with 1194 for Nalanda in one tradition. Jagaddala was sacked in the early thirteenth century, not the eleventh.

nindian-history-144-19.s: Which Pratihara ruler came immediately after Vatsaraja?
nindian-history-144-19.x: The order is Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mihira Bhoja, Mahendrapala I and Mahipala, so Nagabhata II followed Vatsaraja.

nd59782b93a9.s:
Consider the following statements about the order of Rashtrakuta rulers:
1. Dantidurga ruled from 753 to 756.
2. Dhruva ruled before Govinda III.
3. Amoghavarsha I ruled before Govinda III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nd59782b93a9.x: The order is Dantidurga (753-756), Dhruva (780-793), Govinda III (793-814) and Amoghavarsha I (814-878). Amoghavarsha I came after Govinda III.

n20106e8a513.s:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Chalukya ruler Vijayaditya II:
1. He is associated with building 108 Shiva temples.
2. He is linked with the naming of Vijayawada.
3. He composed the Kavirajamarga in Kannada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n20106e8a513.x: Vijayaditya II is associated with 108 Shiva temples and the naming of Vijayawada. Kavirajamarga was written by the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I.

new.s: Which inscription records the election of Gopala as king?
new.x: The Khalimpur inscription of Dharmapala records Gopala's election. The Nalanda copper plate records Devapala's grant of five villages.

new.s: Gopala was elected by the notables to end a state of anarchy known as:
new.x: Gopala was elected in the mid-8th century to end matsyanyaya, the 'law of the jungle'. The Kaivarta revolt came under Ramapala.

new.s: Which Pala ruler installed Chakrayudha on the throne of Kannauj?
new.x: Dharmapala installed Chakrayudha at Kannauj. Devapala is known for the Nalanda grant and Mahipala I for reviving Pala power.

new.s: Besides Nagabhata II, the Pala king Dharmapala was also defeated by which Rashtrakuta ruler?
new.x: Dharmapala was defeated by Dhruva and by Nagabhata II near Monghyr.

new.s: Jagaddala Mahavihara was founded by:
new.x: Jagaddala in Varendra was founded by Ramapala, the last strong Pala ruler. Gopala built Odantapuri and Dharmapala Vikramashila.

new.s: Odantapuri Mahavihara is located at present-day:
new.x: Odantapuri, built by Gopala, was at Bihar Sharif in Bihar.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Vikramashila Mahavihara:
1. It was founded by Dharmapala.
2. It lies in Banka district of Bihar.
3. It was a centre of Tantric (Vajrayana) Buddhism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala and was a Vajrayana centre. It lies at Antichak in Bhagalpur district, not Banka.

new.s: Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by:
new.x: Nalanda was founded by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I in the 5th century AD; the Palas only patronised it.

new.s: The foundation of the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara was laid in:
new.x: Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap laid the foundation of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara on 20 November 1951.

new.s: Taxila, the odd one out among early medieval centres of learning, was the capital of:
new.x: Taxila was an early Buddhist centre and the capital of Gandhara, in present Rawalpindi district of Pakistan.

new.s: Which of the following studied at Taxila?
new.x: Taxila's students included Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya, Charaka and Jivaka. Atisha, Shilabhadra and Dharmakirti belong to the Pala-era mahaviharas.

new.s: Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded which monastery in Tibet?
new.x: Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded the Samye monastery in Tibet.

new.s: Sakya Sri Bhadra, who took Tantric Buddhism to Tibet, was associated with:
new.x: Sakya Sri Bhadra belonged to Jagaddala. Atisha was from Vikramashila and Shantarakshita from Nalanda.

new.s: Who was the head of Nalanda in Harsha's time?
new.x: Shilabhadra headed Nalanda in Harsha's time.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Balaputradeva:
1. He was a Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa.
2. His envoy obtained five villages for his Nalanda monastery from Dharmapala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Balaputradeva was the Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa. The five villages were granted by Devapala, not Dharmapala.

new.s: Pala sculpture was chiefly made in:
new.x: Pala sculpture is known for bronze and black-stone (basalt) images.

new.s: Grand-scale Pala terracotta decoration is best seen at:
new.x: Somapura shows Pala terracotta on a grand scale; Vikramashila has terracotta wall panels.

new.s: Sandhyakar Nandi's Ramacharita deals with which Pala ruler?
new.x: Ramacharita by Sandhyakar Nandi deals with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt.

new.s: Who founded the Sena dynasty of Bengal?
new.x: Samantasena, from Karnataka and a Pala feudatory in Rarh, founded the Sena line. Vijayasena founded independent Sena rule.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The scholar king Ballalasena wrote Danasagara and Adbhutasagara. Jayadeva was Lakshmanasena's poet, and Lakshmanasena was ousted by Bakhtiyar Khilji.

new.s: The Gurjaras are first mentioned in the Harshacharita and in the:
new.x: The Gurjaras are first mentioned in the Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II and Banabhatta's Harshacharita.

new.s: The early seat of the Gurjaras was at:
new.x: Bhinmal in Rajasthan was the early Gurjara seat; Ujjain and then Kannauj (Mahodaya) came later.

new.s: What was the capital of the Pratihara founder Nagabhata I?
new.x: Nagabhata I ruled from Ujjain (Avanti). Kannauj became the capital from Nagabhata II.

new.s: Kannauj, the Pratihara capital from Nagabhata II's time, was also known as:
new.x: Kannauj was also called Mahodaya; the Barah copper plate of Bhoja mentions a camp there.

new.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler defeated the Pratihara king Nagabhata II?
new.x: Nagabhata II was defeated by Govinda III, while his predecessor Vatsaraja lost to Dhruva.

new.s: Which Pratihara ruler bore the title 'Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta'?
new.x: Mahendrapala I (c. 885–910) was styled Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta and patronised Rajashekhara.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mihira Bhoja:
1. He was the son of Ramabhadra.
2. He was the grandson of Nagabhata II.
3. His coins carry a Shaiva legend.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Mihira Bhoja was Ramabhadra's son and Nagabhata II's grandson. His coins carry the Vaishnava legend Adivaraha, not a Shaiva one.

new.s: Besides Adivaraha, which title did Mihira Bhoja bear?
new.x: Mihira Bhoja bore the titles Adivaraha and Prabhasa. Nripatunga and Viranarayana were Amoghavarsha I's, Prabhutavarsha Govinda III's.

new.s: The Arab writer Al-Masudi called the Pratihara king:
new.x: Al-Masudi called the Pratihara king Baura; Juzr is Sulaiman's name for the kingdom, and Balhara was the Arab term for Rashtrakuta kings.

new.s: In which year did Muhammad bin Qasim take Sindh?
new.x: Muhammad bin Qasim took Sindh in 712, defeating and killing Raja Dahir.

new.s: The Gwalior inscription of Mihira Bhoja credits whom with repulsing the mleccha (Arab) army?
new.x: The Gwalior inscription says Nagabhata I repulsed the mleccha army.

new.s: Prabandhachintamani was written by:
new.x: Prabandhachintamani is Merutunga's work, not Rajashekhara's.

new.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler looted Kannauj around 916, defeating the Pratihara Mahipala I?
new.x: Indra III raided Kannauj c. 916, defeating Mahipala I.

new.s: Which breakaway Pratihara feudatory is associated with Khajuraho?
new.x: The Chandelas of Khajuraho were among the feudatories that broke away as Pratihara power declined.

new.s: Which ritual did Dantidurga perform at Ujjayini?
new.x: Dantidurga performed the Hiranyagarbha ritual at Ujjayini (Ujjain).

new.s: Dantidurga overthrew which Badami Chalukya ruler?
new.x: Dantidurga, a former Chalukya feudatory, overthrew Kirtivarman II of Badami.

new.s: Dantidurga's inscription at Ellora is found in the:
new.x: Dantidurga's inscription is in Ellora's Dashavatara cave; the Kailasa temple (Cave 16) was built later by Krishna I.

new.s: Govinda III's campaign up to the Himalayas is recorded in the:
new.x: The Sanjan and Radhanpur plates record Govinda III's northern campaign.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dhruva – first Rashtrakuta to go north
Krishna III – Kailasa temple at Ellora
new.x: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by Krishna I, not Krishna III, who won at Takkolam.

new.s: What was the early seat of the Rashtrakutas?
new.x: Elapura (Ellora) was the early seat; Manyakheta was built later by Amoghavarsha I.

new.s: 'Prabhutavarsha' was a title of which Rashtrakuta ruler?
new.x: Prabhutavarsha was Govinda III's title; Nripatunga and Viranarayana were Amoghavarsha I's.

new.s: Which Arab writer called the Balhara the 'king of kings'?
new.x: Ibn Khurdadhbih called the Balhara the greatest king of India, 'king of kings'.

new.s: In which year did Sulaiman visit in Amoghavarsha I's reign?
new.x: Sulaiman's account dates to 851, in Amoghavarsha I's reign.

new.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler defeated the Rashtrakuta Krishna II?
new.x: Gunaga Vijayaditya III beat Krishna II. Vijayaditya II fought 108 battles and Vijayaditya I was Dantidurga's contemporary.

new.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi to Dhruva?
new.x: Defeated by Dhruva, Vishnuvardhana IV gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi to him.

new.s: At Takkolam (949 CE), Krishna III was aided by the Western Gangas and the:
new.x: Krishna III fought at Takkolam with the Western Gangas and the Vaidumbas against the Cholas of Parantaka I.

new.s: Ganitasarasangraha, a Sanskrit work on mathematics, was written by:
new.x: Ganitasarasangraha is by Mahaviracharya.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Rashtrakuta-era literature:
1. Kavirajamarga by Amoghavarsha I is in Kannada.
2. Prashnottara Ratnamalika is in Sanskrit.
3. Nalachampu was written by Halayudha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Kavirajamarga is in Kannada and Prashnottara Ratnamalika in Sanskrit. Nalachampu is by Trivikrama Bhatta; Halayudha wrote Kavirahasya.

new.s: Which of the following poet – patron pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Pampa was patronised by Arikesari II of Vemulavada. Ponna's patron was Krishna III and Ranna's Tailapa II.

new.s: Gadayuddha was written by:
new.x: Ranna, patronised by Tailapa II, wrote Gadayuddha.

new.s: The Paramara Siyaka II defeated which Rashtrakuta ruler and sacked Manyakheta?
new.x: Siyaka II defeated Khottiga on the Narmada and sacked Manyakheta.
